title: Nasdaq sinks 5.5% on AI fears — chipmakers fell far more than buyers
summary: The Nasdaq's worst day since April 2025: memory and chip suppliers fell far harder than the companies buying from them, and Ada and Alan argue over whether election permission risk or leverage did it. Then Geoffrey Hinton's dated Chornobyl forecast and his FDA-for-AI ask, set against Three Mile Island and drug-law history, and what Claude's new read-only Personal Finance feature can actually see.

topics: AI trade selloff, Nov 5 2026: Nasdaq Composite -5.5% (worst since April 2025), Nasdaq 100 -6.3%, S&P -4.4%, Philadelphia semiconductor index -12.3% (worst since March 2020); SanDisk -22%, Micron/WD/AMD -17%, Seagate -16%, Arm -13%, Qualcomm -9.5%, Nvidia -9.2% (~$450B), hyperscalers only -2 to -4%. Causes argued: blue wave and data-center permission risk, Qualcomm/Arm earnings, rates and debt, leverage. Kospi -8%+ with halt and TAIEX -9% on Friday.

Geoffrey Hinton's Guardian interview (Robert Booth, Nov 3 2026): 'better off never developing it'; dated forecast of a Chornobyl-type AI-enabled attack later this year or next; Hugging Face incident as Three Mile Island warning shot; FDA-style approval with statistical evidence; no trust in Altman; 'still in control'. Taught against NRC's TMI account and FDA law history.

Claude Personal Finance beta (Nov 5 2026): Plaid-linked, read-only, US Pro/Max/Ultra; sees balances, limits and up to two years of transactions; hub chats not used for training, outside the hub privacy settings apply; 'first step' toward working with licensed firms.

lore.note: Alan's memory-price sore spot developed again: faced with memory stocks falling hardest in the Nov 5 selloff and the 'cheap RAM for Christmas' hope, he insisted a share price doesn't free up a wafer, and conceded he hadn't considered that depressed stocks could mean less new capacity and costlier memory.

Alan says the Nov 5 selloff was mostly leverage coming out and will concede only when a big cloud company actually cuts a spending number; Ada holds that permission is the lasting part and that permits will move first. He also wrote down a falsifier for Hinton's forecast: by Dec 31, 2027, an attack credibly attributed to AI that takes down a grid or financial system for about a week. Unresolved.
